item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot app: Branded footer customization
item.description:
Updated September 17, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

We’re introducing a new co-branding capability that will allow organizations to display a branded footer at the bottom of the Chat screen in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app. This update will enable admins to add their organization’s logo to their users’ Microsoft 365 Copilot app, helping users confirm they are using their trusted, work-managed Copilot experience.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 555852.

[When this will happen]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out August 2026 (previously mid-July) and is expected to complete by mid-September 2026 (previously end of July).

[How this will affect your organization]

Who is affected

  • All Microsoft 365 tenants using the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

What will happen

  • Admins will be able to upload a logo in the Microsoft 365 admin center to customize the footer in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • The footer will use the same logo configured in your organization’s theme for other Microsoft 365 apps. Only the logo will be used; other theme settings will not apply in this release.

  • Admins can choose a footer label: Approved by, Provided by, or Managed by. Selecting No label will display the logo without a label.
  • This feature will be off by default and will require admin configuration.
  • There will be no user impact unless an admin enables the footer.

[What you can do to prepare]

No action will be required unless you want to enable the branded footer.

Admins who want to configure this feature should:

  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Org settings > Custom theme and open your default theme.
  • Confirm that your organization’s logo is configured in the Logos tab. This is the same logo used for your organization’s branding in other Microsoft 365 apps.
  • Open the Copilot Chat tab and select Add your brand to Copilot Chat footer area.
  • In the Footer style dropdown, choose No label, Approved by, Provided by, or Managed by.
  • Save your changes to display your logo in the branded footer in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

Please note: The footer currently uses your organization's default theme and applies to all users. Targeting different logos to specific user groups will be supported in a later update.

For configuration guidance: Customize the theme for your organization | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Edge: IE mode is supported through at least the end of 2029, plan your migration
item.description:
[What and why] 

Internet Explorer (IE) mode in Microsoft Edge remains supported through at least the end of 2029, as first announced in 2021. Microsoft is sharing this reminder so admins can plan migrations for legacy websites and applications that still depend on IE mode. Application modernization projects can take years to complete depending on the number and complexity of dependencies, so early planning reduces the risk of disruption later.

[Rollout schedule]

This is a reminder, not a rollout of a new feature or capability. IE mode support continues through at least the end of 2029 across Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD environments. Microsoft will provide at least one year of notice before retiring IE mode.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that use IE mode in Microsoft Edge for legacy websites or applications

Organizations that do not use IE mode are not affected.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Edge

What will happen

  • If your organization does not use IE mode, there is no impact and no action is required.
  • If your organization uses IE mode, you can continue using it while you modernize affected websites and applications.
  • Support for IE mode continues through at least the end of 2029, but modernization projects may take years to complete.
  • This message does not change your current IE mode configuration or require you to disable IE mode immediately. It is intended to help you identify dependencies and plan migration work before the end of the current support period.

[Action required and recommendations] 

If your organization no longer uses IE mode in Microsoft Edge, no action is required.

If your organization still depends on IE mode:

  • Inventory your IE mode dependencies. Identify the business-critical websites and applications that still require IE mode. Review your existing Enterprise Mode Site List and current usage to build your inventory.
  • Assess modernization options. Determine whether each application should be updated, rehosted, replaced, or rebuilt using modern technologies and services.
  • Request assistance if needed. Microsoft App Assure provides no cost assistance for eligible customers experiencing application compatibility issues with Microsoft Edge and IE mode.

Planning early can help your organization identify migration risks and reduce the likelihood of disruption as you move away from IE mode dependencies.

Learn more

  • Microsoft App Assure: App Compatibility Support | Microsoft 365
  • Lifecycle FAQ - Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Retirement Notice of Learning Coach Agent in M365 Copilot
item.description:
Updated September 17, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

The Learning Coach Agent (Learning Coach) in Microsoft 365 Copilot will have a transition banner to Learning Agent starting from the first week of October 2026 and will be retired on the last week of December 2026. Users will no longer be able to access the Learning Coach agent through Microsoft 365 Copilot from October 2026. Existing Learning Coach experiences, entry points, and associated functionality will be removed as part of this deprecation in the last week of December 2026. Customers who rely on Learning Coach for learning recommendations, skill development guidance, or personalized learning support should transition to Learning Agent (https://aka.ms/learning-agent) before the retirement date.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Learning Agent Transition banner In Learning Coach

Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on early October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

Learning Coach Retirement and removal from M365 Copilot

Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on late December 2026 and expect to complete by early-January 2027.

[Impact on your organization:]

Customer Impact:

  • Currently, the agent is no longer discoverable by new users and cannot be searched for or installed. Existing users can continue accessing the agent through the agent tray until the first week of October. After that, the agent will have a transition banner informing users about Learning Agent. After December 2026, Learning Coach will no longer be accessible to all users through Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Organizational Impact:

  • Administrators will continue to see and manage the agent in the Microsoft Admin Center (MAC) until the last week of December. After that point, the agent will be completely removed from MAC and will no longer be available for administration or deployment. Organizations relying on the agent will need to transition users to Learning Agent (https://aka.ms/learning-agent) before these deadlines to avoid disruption.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

    1. Communicate the retirement of the Learning Coach Agent to all users within the tenant and provide clear timelines for its deprecation.
    2. Advise users to review and save any important conversations or information from the Learning Coach Agent before it becomes unavailable.
    3. Update internal training materials, documentation, and support resources to reference the Learning Agent as the recommended alternative.
    4. Guide users to transition their learning and upskilling activities to the Learning Agent (https://aka.ms/learning-agent)

    Documentation:

    • Learning Agent End user Documentation: Overview of Learning Agent | Microsoft Support

    Learning Agent Admin Documentation:Overview of Learning Agent | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Project Operations - Improve NTE reliability and validation coverage
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to improve Not-To-Exceed (NTE) reliability and validation coverage in Dynamics 365 Project Operations. This feature will reach public preview on September 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature provides consistent control over NTE limits across every billable type, so users avoid over-billing, and protect revenue.

The core capabilities of this feature include:
  • Extends NTE validation beyond time entries to include expense, material, and fixed-price components.
  • Enhances the Invoice Confirmation Service to block confirmation when Total Billed + Unbilled Committed > NTE Amount.
  • Fixes bugs where NTE status fails to update on approval records due to custom plugin conflicts, ensuring deterministic results.
What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Improve NTE reliability and validation coverage.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot Analytics: Data export public preview for Copilot metrics in the Copilot dashboard
item.description:
Updated September 17, 2026: We have updated the timeline. This post has also been updated to remind customers that this feature is default-on for Copilot Dashboard users with full company-level data access. The export output remains de-identified, with each user represented by a hashed ID. Please review and take any actions as appropriate for your organization. Thank you for your patience.

This MC post is associated with Roadmap ID 500872.

[Introduction:]

To support deeper analysis of Copilot adoption, Microsoft is introducing a new export capability in the Copilot Dashboard. This feature allows dashboard users with company-level access to download de-identified Copilot usage metrics, aggregated by user and week, from the past six months. Organizations can use this data to track adoption trends, optimize licensing, and support AI transformation strategies.

This feature requires at least 50 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and applies to the Viva Insights web app.

[When this will happen:]

  • Public Preview: Begins in early October 2026 (previously early December 2025), completes by late October 2026 (previously late December 2025).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Begins in mid-October 2026 (previously early September), completes by end of October 2026 (previously late September).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

Copilot Dashboard users with full company-level data access, including senior leaders (as identified in Entra ID), admin-assigned company-level users, delegates with company-level access, as well as global analysts and admins. 

Note: Group managers with data access limited to their own teams will not have access to this feature.

What will happen:

  • Users will be able to export de-identified, row-level Copilot usage metrics from the dashboard.
  • The dataset includes weekly, user-level metrics from the past six months.
  • The export supports Copilot usage analysis across apps (such as Word, Excel, Teams), and includes two attributes: Organization, and Job function.
  • Organizations can use the data to track usage patterns, generate insights to inform adoption strategies, optimize licensing, and measure ROI.
  • The feature is enabled by default for eligible users.
  • Admins can manage access via Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) settings, under Module: Viva Insights; Feature: Copilot Metrics Export.
  • No impact to user workflow unless accessed by eligible users.

Screenshot 2 - Example of output: 

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • Review the assignment of the Copilot dashboard users with full company-wide data access and adjust VFAM policies as needed.
  • Communicate the upcoming feature to eligible users so they know what to expect.
  • No admin setup is required to start using the export.

item.title: [stayInformed] Copilot Studio - Billing for GitHub Copilot harness built agents begins September 1, 2026
item.description:
Update: The rollout of the usage-based billing model completed on September 15, 2026. Admins will begin to see usage-based billing changes in your environment(s) following this date.

Beginning September 1, 2026, the grace period for existing agents and workflows built using the GitHub Copilot harness in Copilot Studio will end. These agents and workflows will begin consuming Copilot Credits under the usage-based billing model.

This applies to GitHub Copilot harness agents and workflows created before August 3, 2026, including those created in Dev or Trial environments. Both maker AI authoring activities and runtime execution will consume Copilot Credits. Standard harness and Copilot Chat harness agents are not affected.

How does this affect me?
Starting September 1, 2026, GitHub Copilot harness agents and workflows in your environment will consume Copilot Credits. Consumption information will be available through existing Power Platform admin center (PPAC) reporting and capacity management experiences.

Historical non-billed Copilot Credits data is available in the Power Platform admin center to help you understand current usage patterns. In PPAC, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents. This information is directional only and should not be interpreted as a billing estimate or future cost.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

Optionally, we recommend:

  • Administrators review historical Copilot Credits consumption and identify active GitHub Copilot harness agents and workflows before billing begins.
  • Administrators manage GitHub Copilot harness consumption by allocating credits to environments, controlling access to the shared tenant credit pool, monitoring usage in PPAC, and using Azure budgets and alerts for pay-as-you-go spending.

Learn More:

  • Manage costs for agents powered by the GitHub Copilot harness
  • Manage Copilot Credits and capacity for Copilot Studio
  • Manage Copilot Credits allocations programmatically
  • Identify all GitHub Copilot harness agents that have been created in your organization

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Commerce - Print receipts using Adyen payment terminal printers
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to print receipts using the built-in printer on supported Adyen payment terminals in Dynamics 365 Commerce. This feature will reach public preview on October 2, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature enables organizations to design and manage receipt formats in Commerce headquarters and print them directly from an Adyen payment terminal, without requiring a separate receipt printer.

When this feature is enabled, administrators can configure receipt formats by using the existing receipt designer in Commerce headquarters and associate the receipt profile with the hardware profile used by the Adyen payment terminal. After a customer completes a payment, the terminal can print the receipt using its built-in printer.

This capability can reduce the need for dedicated receipt printers and allows store associates to accept payments and provide receipts from a single device.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [planForChange] Brand Skill support now available in PPT Copilot [Desktop]
item.description:
[What and why:]

Brand managers will be able to upload custom presentation skills as Markdown (.md) files to Brand Kit and share them across their organization for use with Copilot in PowerPoint. This capability helps organizations provide reusable, organization-approved instructions that guide presentation creation, supporting more consistent and efficient content development.

This change advances personal and team productivity by embedding reusable presentation guidance into the tools employees use to create presentations.

[Rollout schedule:]

Frontier: We will begin rolling out mid-September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

General Availability, Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in late September 2026 and expect to complete by the end of September 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Brand managers who create, manage, and publish organizational Brand Kits.
  • Users in organizations where a Brand Kit containing a custom presentation skill has been published and who have access to Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • The product team should confirm applicable licensing and whether additional eligibility requirements apply.

Platforms and services:

  • Microsoft 365 Brand Kit
  • Microsoft Copilot
  • Microsoft PowerPoint - Desktop

What will happen:

  • Brand managers will be able to upload a custom presentation skill as a Markdown (.md) or .zip file to Brand Kit.
  • Brand managers will be able to publish the skill for use by people in their organization.
  • Eligible users will be able to use the published skill with Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • The skill can provide reusable instructions to guide how Copilot creates presentations.
  • The feature requires a Brand manager to upload and publish a skill. It is not automatically activated merely because the capability becomes available.

[Action required and recommendations:]

  • Review who is assigned as a Brand manager through the Enterprise Brand Manager policy.
  • Identify the people responsible for writing, reviewing, approving, and maintaining presentation skills.
  • Establish governance for security, privacy, accessibility, legal, and brand review.
  • Test skills with representative presentation scenarios before publishing them broadly.
  • Communicate the availability of published skills to users of Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • Update internal Brand Kit and Copilot documentation.
  • Review published skills periodically and remove or replace outdated instructions.
  • Review Microsoft documentation: Brand Skill support for Copilot in PowerPoint.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • This change provides eligible users with a new way to interact with generative AI by using organization-published instructions with Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • This change introduces organization-published instructions that can guide Copilot when users create presentations.
  • Brand Kit publishing is governed through the Enterprise Brand Manager policy and a mail-enabled security group. Confirm that presentation skills use the same controls without additional configuration.
  • Confirm storage, retention, audit logging, Purview behavior, user-level disablement, third-party integration, and GDPR data-subject-request implications before publication.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Purview: permissions audit log improvements
item.description:
[What and why]

To improve transparency and troubleshooting for Microsoft Purview role-based access control (RBAC), we are enhancing audit logging for permission checks performed in the Microsoft Purview portal. These new audit records will provide administrators with clearer visibility into role and scoped-role authorization decisions, helping them investigate access issues and better understand how access evaluations are performed.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 569363.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late September 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Purview administrators and compliance administrators who review audit logs for access investigations and troubleshooting

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview portal
  • Microsoft Purview Audit

What will happen

  • New audit records will be generated when access checks are performed in the Microsoft Purview portal.
  • Two new audit operations will be available:
    • CheckUsersInRoles
    • CheckUserInRolesWithScopes
  • Administrators will be able to review these audit records as part of SecurityComplianceRBAC audit activities.
  • The enhancement is enabled by default and requires no configuration.
  • Audit records will only be generated for access checks that occur after the feature is deployed.
  • No historical or retroactive audit records will be created for prior access checks.
  • There is no impact for organizations.

RBAC audit-CheckUserInRolesWithScopes:

RBAC audit-checkusersinroles:

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that administrators:

  • Review internal monitoring and audit procedures to determine whether the new audit activities should be included in access investigations.
  • Inform compliance and security teams about the availability of the new audit operations.
  • Update any internal documentation or reporting processes that reference Microsoft Purview RBAC audit data.

Learn more

  • Permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable audit logging capabilities?The change enhances audit logging capabilities by adding two new audit operations.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Administrators gain additional audit visibility into RBAC access evaluation outcomes, improving monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: New centralized experience for organizing important resources in chats and channels
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing a more consistent way for users to access and manage important resources in Microsoft Teams chats and channels. Users will be able to pin frequently used resources directly below the chat or channel header, pin multiple messages alongside other resources, and organize them into folders. On Microsoft Teams mobile, users will be able to access shared resources and folders by tapping the chat or channel header. This change will help users stay organized and provide them with a centralized location to quickly find, access, and manage important resources.

As part of this update, the In this chat and In this channel panes will be removed. Existing resources within these panes will be accessible through the new resource management experience.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late September 2026 and is expected to complete by early October 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who access or manage resources in Microsoft Teams chats and channels.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft Teams mobile

What will happen

  • Users will have a centralized location to find, access, and manage important resources.
  • Users will be able to pin frequently used resources directly below the chat or channel header, pin multiple messages alongside other resources, and organize them into folders.
  • On mobile devices, users will be able to access shared resources and folders by tapping the chat or channel header.
  • The In this chat and In this channel panes will be removed; existing resources within these panes will be accessed and managed through the updated experience.

[Action required and recommendations]

No administrative action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Inform users about the updated resource pinning and management experience.
  • Update any internal training or support documentation that references the In this chat and In this channel panes.

[Learn more]

We will update this post with new documentation.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Loading Power Query data to Python in Excel Web: Retirement
item.description:
[What and why:]

Microsoft is retiring support for loading Power Query data into the Python runtime in Excel for the web. After this change, users will no longer be able to use Power Query as a data source for Python in Excel when working in Excel for the web. This retirement aligns investments in Python in Excel with supported experiences and does not affect Excel for Windows desktop.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Retirement date: October 16, 2026

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who use Python in Excel with Power Query data sources in Excel for the web.

Platforms affected:

  • Excel for the web

What will happen:

  • Beginning October 16, 2026, users will no longer be able to load Power Query data into the Python runtime in Excel for the web.
  • Workflows that depend on combining Power Query and Python in Excel for the web will no longer function as expected.
  • No changes are being made to Python in Excel experiences in Excel for Windows desktop.
  • Users can continue to import external data by using Power Query and analyze data with Python in Excel on supported desktop experiences.

[Action Required / Recommendations:]

  • No administrative action is required.
  • Identify users and business processes that rely on Power Query data being loaded into Python in Excel for the web.
  • Notify affected users of the retirement and expected workflow impact.
  • Review affected solutions and consider transitioning those workflows to Excel for Windows desktop where this capability remains available.
  • Update internal training, documentation, and support materials as needed.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Viva Engage: Email updates for frontline users without an active Exchange mailbox
item.description:
Updated September 16, 2026: We have updated the content timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

Viva Engage will stop sending email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination. Previously, email notifications could still be attempted for these users, resulting in repeated delivery retries, increased load on email systems, and, in some cases, delays to important business communications.

This change reduces unnecessary email traffic, improves delivery efficiency, and helps ensure important communications are delivered reliably and on time.

Users with supported mailbox configurations, including cloud mailboxes, on-premises mailboxes, shared mailboxes, and other routable email destinations, will continue to receive Viva Engage email notifications as expected.

Notifications delivered through supported channels such as Microsoft Teams remain unaffected.

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins end of September 2026 (previously mid-September) and is expected to complete by end of October 2026 (previously end of September).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Microsoft 365 admins managing Viva Engage users and mailbox configurations.

What will happen:

  • Viva Engage will no longer attempt to send email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Users with cloud, on-premises, shared, or other supported mailbox configurations will continue to receive email notifications as expected.
  • This change does not affect the existing email notification experience for users with a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Notifications delivered through Microsoft Teams or other supported channels are not impacted.
  • The change is enabled by default and applies automatically.
  • Organizations may see:
    • Reduced load on email systems and gateways.
    • Fewer retry attempts for undeliverable messages.
    • Improved email delivery efficiency and reliability.

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • No action is required.
  • Review your Exchange Online licensing configuration to identify users without mailbox access.
  • Evaluate your notification strategy (e.g., Teams vs. Email) for frontline workers.
  • Inform helpdesk and user support teams of the expected behavior change.
  • Update internal documentation if email notifications are referenced for frontline users.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Alters how existing customer data is processed: Email notifications to users without mailboxes are no longer attempted, reducing unnecessary processing of undeliverable messages.
  • No other compliance impacts identified.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint: Guide Presentation Creation with Notes Steering and Strict Brand Adherence
item.description:
[What and why:]

We're introducing two new Brand Kit template settings in Microsoft 365 that help organizations create more consistent, on-brand presentations with Copilot in PowerPoint.

Strict brand adherence (Strict Mode) allows Brand Managers to control whether Copilot can create new layouts or must use only approved template and slide master layouts. When enabled, Copilot follows the template exactly and does not add or remove placeholders or create new layouts.

Allow note instructions (Notes Steering) enables Brand Managers to add instructions directly in template speaker notes to guide how Copilot generates presentations. For example, organizations can instruct Copilot to always include a specific slide, preserve branded content, maintain slide order, control text density, or tailor content for a specific audience

These settings can be used independently or together to help organizations generate more predictable, consistent, and brand-aligned presentations.

[Rollout schedule:]

Available now.

[Impact on your organization:]

These capabilities give organizations greater control over how Copilot creates presentations from branded templates.

With Notes Steering, organizations can embed reusable guidance directly into templates, helping ensure presentations consistently follow branding, messaging, and content requirements without requiring users to repeat instructions in every prompt. With Strict Mode enabled, Copilot uses only approved template layouts and slide masters, helping organizations maintain presentation standards and reduce deviations from approved brand designs. This is especially valuable for customer-facing, executive, regulatory, or other business-critical presentations where brand consistency is important.

Together, these settings help deliver more predictable, on-brand PowerPoint presentations while reducing manual editing and review effort.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

No action is required to use these capabilities.

However, organizations that want greater control over presentation generation should designate Brand Managers and ensure they have permissions to manage Brand Kits. Only Brand Kit owners and Brand Managers can configure template settings such as Strict Brand Adherence and Allow Note Instructions.

To take advantage of these capabilities, Brand Managers can update existing Brand Kit templates or upload new templates configured with Notes Steering and Strict Mode settings.

item.title: [stayInformed] Enhanced security and access controls for Outlook attachments

  • Users out of compliance will be blocked from attachments. If a user's session no longer satisfies a Conditional Access policy — for example, a non-compliant device, a blocked location, or a network change that triggers CAE re-evaluation — attachment operations will be blocked.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication
item.description:
Updated September 15, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

Passkeys became the default authentication experience in Microsoft Entra on September 1, 2026. Telecom-based methods (SMS and voice) will transition to customer-configured providers through the Microsoft Security Store.

The AI era demands stronger, phishing-resistant authentication. We are making passkeys the default authentication experience in Microsoft Entra to help customers securely adopt AI at scale.

As part of this transition, SMS and voice will no longer be available as multifactor authentication methods starting February 1, 2027. SMS and voice do not offer sufficient levels of security in comparison to passkeys. Traditional authentication methods including passwords, SMS one-time passcodes, and voice-based verification remain vulnerable to phishing, interception, and social engineering attacks.

We strongly recommend moving away from telephony-based authentication methods to improve security and prevent identity attacks. Passkeys are included in all Microsoft Entra plans, so making this critical security change comes at no additional cost for you.

While we recommend adopting passkeys for phishing-resistant authentication as quickly as possible, we also recognize that some customers may have business needs that make an immediate transition impractical. In such cases, customers may continue to use SMS and voice by selecting a telecom provider in the Microsoft Security Store.

[Rollout schedule]

  1. September 1, 2026: Rollout began. Changes may take time to reach all tenants and will be deployed gradually.
  2. Passkeys will be automatically enabled for users currently enabled for SMS or voice.
  3. Registration Campaign will be set to Microsoft-Managed targeting passkeys for all users in eligible tenants.
  4. Users will be prompted to register a passkey during MFA sign-in; users will be able to skip.
  5. September 18th, 2026:
  6. Review the telecom providers and related information available through the Microsoft Security Store to evaluate which option best meets your regional and compliance requirements.
  7. October 30, 2026:
  8. Customers who need to continue to use SMS or voice will be able to choose from a list of telecom providers available through the Microsoft Security Store.
  9. February 1, 2027:
  10. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will be retired.
  11. Only customer-configured telecom providers will support SMS and voice going forward.
  12. Passkeys become the default, recommended authentication method.
  13. July 1, 2027:
  14. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will be retired for Global Admins and external users
  15. Only customer-configured telecom providers will support SMS and voice for these users going forward

If no action is taken, tenants relying only on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice may experience sign-in disruptions after February 1, 2027.


[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  1. All Microsoft Entra ID tenants enabled for SMS or voice authentication
  2. Users enabled for SMS or voice

Platforms and services

  1. Microsoft Entra ID
  2. Multifactor authentication
  3. Microsoft Security Store

What will happen

  1. Passkeys will be automatically enabled for eligible users and Registration Campaign for passkeys will be set to Microsoft Managed state starting September 1, 2026.
  2. Users will be prompted during MFA sign-in to register a passkey; users can skip the prompt.
  3. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will be retired for most users on February 1, 2027, and for Global Administrators and external users on July 1, 2027.
  4. Organizations that still require telephony methods must configure a telecom provider in the Microsoft Security Store.
  5. Tenants that do not configure a provider and continue relying on Microsoft telephony will face SMS and voice authentication disruptions after retirement.

[Action required and recommendations]

Admins should take the following steps:

  1. Prepare for passkeys
  2. Plan to transition users to passkeys and communicate upcoming registration prompts.
  3. Decide if SMS or voice is still required
  4. If SMS or voice is still needed, you must configure a customer-managed telecom provider. We recommend completing setup at least 4 weeks before the February 1 enforcement to allow sufficient time for testing and a cautious transition.
  5. Set up a telecom provider before February 1, 2027
  6. SMS and voice will only work after this date if a customer-configured telecom provider is enabled.
  7. Use temporary opt-out if needed
  8. A temporary opt-out will be available for the September 1, 2026 through February 1, 2027 changes. This allows you to delay passkey and Registration Campaign enablement while you complete transition activities, such as configuring customer-managed telecom providers or migrating to other authentication methods.
  9. After February 1, 2027, passkey enablement will be enforced for all users in scope.

Additional documentation and more information will be available on Microsoft Learn and the Tech Community.

For more information please visit: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-sms-voice-retirement more

Learn more:

  1. Deploy passkey adoption campaigns with the Conditional Access Optimization Agent | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  2. Get started with phishing-resistant passwordless authentication deployment in Microsoft Entra ID | Authentication | Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  3. It's Time to Hang Up on Phone Transports for Authentication | Microsoft Entra Blog

item.title: [planForChange] [Whiteboard] Legacy Whiteboard migration to OneDrive
item.description:
Updated September 15, 2026: This message does not apply to Government customers. We apologize for the confusion, and you can safely disregard this message.

[What and why:]

Microsoft Whiteboard is completing its transition from legacy Azure-backed storage to OneDrive-backed Whiteboards. Organizations that still have legacy Azure-based Whiteboards must migrate them to OneDrive-backed storage before migration tooling is retired - September 25, 2026. After September 25, 2026, remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated and can be only exported until October 16, 2026. After October 16, 2026, any remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.

Key dates

  1. Before September 25, 2026: Users can still trigger migration, retry failed migrations, and export important content.
  2. September 25, 2026: Migration tooling is retired. Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated, but can still be viewed and exported until October 16, 2026.
  3. October 16, 2026: Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
  4. November 30, 2026: Legacy Azure Whiteboard service shuts down.

[Rollout schedule:]

Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on late September 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

This change impacts organizations that still have legacy Azure-based Microsoft Whiteboards that have not yet been migrated to OneDrive-backed storage.

After September 25, 2026:

  • Users will no longer be able to migrate remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards.
  • Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated, but can still be viewed and exported until October 16, 2026.
  • Organizations that have not completed migration risk losing access to business content stored in legacy Whiteboards.

After October 16, 2026:

  • Any remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
  • Enterprise users should access Microsoft Whiteboard through Teams and supported web experiences.

Organizations that have already completed migration to OneDrive-backed Whiteboards will not experience changes to existing OneDrive-backed content. New Whiteboards are already created in OneDrive-backed storage.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Admins should take the following actions immediately:

  • Inventory remaining legacy Whiteboards: Use the WhiteboardAdmin PowerShell module to identify Azure-based Whiteboards that still require migration.
  • Communicate with affected users:
  • Notify Whiteboard owners of the migration deadline (September 25, 2026) and deletion deadline (October 16, 2026).
  • Encourage users to migrate, export, or preserve any business-critical content before the deadlines.
  • Validate migration completion: Review migration status and confirm that important Whiteboards, permissions, and user access have been successfully migrated and remain accessible in OneDrive-backed storage.
  • Plan for large-scale migrations: For inactive users, orphaned Whiteboards, or large migration volumes, consider using the administrator-driven migration approach documented by Microsoft Whiteboard engineering.
  • Update internal guidance: Update user training materials, help documentation, and support procedures to direct users to Microsoft Whiteboard in Teams and supported web experiences rather than standalone applications.
  • Act before migration tooling is retired: After September 25, 2026, migration tooling will no longer be available, and no further migration path will exist for remaining legacy Whiteboards.

item.title: [planForChange] Support for Office LTSC 2021, and additional apps will end on October 13, 2026
item.description:
[What and why:]

As previously communicated, support for Office LTSC 2021 will end on October 13, 2026. After that date, no further updates, security fixes, or technical support will be available for this version of Office. While the applications may continue to function, using unsupported software could lead to potential security risks, compliance risks, system incompatibilities, and other issues.

Support for Visio LTSC 2021, Microsoft Project LTSC 2021 and several other products will also end on October 13, 2026. Organizations using these products should upgrade as soon as possible to maintain security, compliance, and performance.

[Rollout schedule:]

We will begin rolling out mid-October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

After end of support, Office LTSC 2021 suites and standalones will no longer receive security updates or other fixes, and no technical assistance will be available for devices still running them. Continuing to use unsupported software can expose your organization to security and compliance risks and may impact service reliability and performance.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

To mitigate these risks while maintaining access to desktop Office apps, we recommend upgrading devices to a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 suite that includes Microsoft 365 Apps (for enterprise or for business). Microsoft 365 Apps provides always-up-to-date versions of familiar apps like Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for desktop, mobile, and web with continuous support under the Modern Lifecycle Policy, and is eligible for use with the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on.

  • Enterprises should look to Microsoft 365 E3, Office 365 E3, or Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
  • Organizations with fewer than 300 users should look to Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Microsoft 365 Business Standard, or Microsoft 365 Apps for business.

For scenarios that require a fully disconnected solution, we recommend upgrading to Office LTSC 2024. Office LTSC 2024 is Microsoft’s current supported on-premises version of Office for commercial customers and will be supported until October 2029 under the Fixed Lifecycle Policy.

Take steps to prepare for this transition with the following resources:

  1. Read the upgrade guidance for an overview of how to move from Office LTSC 2021 to Microsoft 365 Apps. 
  2. Consider engaging Microsoft FastTrack, a Microsoft support service, for moving to Microsoft 365. 

Take action before October 13, 2026, to help maintain security, compliance, and access to supported Office apps.
